# Design Tic-Tac-Toe | | | |---|---| | **Difficulty** | Medium | | **Pattern** | Design · State machine · Win detection | | **Interview heat** | ★★★☆☆ | | **Asked at** | Amazon, Google, Meta, Uber | ## Problem Statement Implement a Tic-Tac-Toe board. - Player 1 (`X`) always moves first, player 2 (`O`) always moves second, and the players alternate. - A move places the current player's mark on an empty cell of the 3×3 board. - After every move the game reports its state: `1` (X wins), `2` (O wins), `3` (draw), `0` (still running) or `-1` (illegal move: the cell is taken, out of range, or the game is already over). ## Input Format ``` n r1 c1 r2 c2 ... rn cn ``` - `n` — number of moves. - `ri ci` — the row and the column of the move, both between 0 and 2. The program prints one line per move with the state of the game. ## Sample Input ``` 5 0 0 1 1 0 1 1 0 0 2 ``` ## Expected Output ``` 0 0 0 0 1 ``` The moves are X(0,0), O(1,1), X(0,1), O(1,0), X(0,2) — the last one completes the top row, so X wins. ## Approach — a 9 cell board plus the player to move State is tiny: nine cells, each `0` (empty), `1` (X) or `2` (O), plus the index of the player whose turn it is. Everything else is derived. **Win detection.** There are exactly eight winning lines: three rows, three columns and two diagonals. After a move only the player who just moved can have won, so eight constant-time checks are enough — no need to re-check the whole board. **Alternating turns.** After a successful move the player flips with `nextPlayer = 3 - nextPlayer`. **Terminal states.** A win or a full board ends the game; further moves are rejected with `-1`. ## Dry Run The board is printed row by row; `X` is player 1, `O` is player 2, `.` is empty. | Step | Move | Board before | Player | Action | Board after | Winning line? | Output | |---:|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `0 0` | `
. . .
. . .
. . .` | X | write X at (0,0) | `X . .
. . .
. . .` | no | `0` | | 2 | `1 1` | `X . .
. . .
. . .` | O | write O at (1,1) | `X . .
. . O
. . .` | no | `0` | | 3 | `0 1` | `X . .
. . O
. . .` | X | write X at (0,1) | `X X .
. . O
. . .` | no | `0` | | 4 | `1 0` | `X X .
. . O
. . .` | O | write O at (1,0) | `X X .
O . O
. . .` | no | `0` | | 5 | `0 2` | `X X .
O . O
. . .` | X | write X at (0,2) | `X X X
O . O
. . .` | **row 0** | `1` | ### The eight winning lines ``` rows: (0,1,2) (3,4,5) (6,7,8) columns: (0,3,6) (1,4,7) (2,5,8) diags: (0,4,8) (2,4,6) ``` With the board flattened row by row, a line is a triple of indices — that is why the code stores the board in a flat `int[9]`. ## Java Solution See [`DesignTicTacToe.java`](./DesignTicTacToe.java). ```java public int move(int row, int col) { if (finished || row < 0 || row > 2 || col < 0 || col > 2) { return -1; } int index = row * 3 + col; if (board[index] != 0) { return -1; // the cell is taken } board[index] = nextPlayer; if (hasWon(nextPlayer)) { finished = true; return nextPlayer; } if (isFull()) { finished = true; return 3; // draw } nextPlayer = 3 - nextPlayer; return 0; } ``` ## Complexity | | Value | Why | |---|---|---| | **Time** | O(1) per move | 8 lines × 3 cells, plus a 9 cell scan for a draw | | **Space** | O(1) | a 3×3 board | ## Interview Notes **Follow-ups to raise yourself:** - *"How would you detect the winner in O(1) per move for a 5×5 board?"* → keep a counter per row, column and diagonal and increment the ones the move touches; a counter that reaches 5 means a win. - *"How would you support a board game with undo?"* → keep a stack of (cell, previous mark) pairs. - *"What if the board is huge (1e9 × 1e9)?"* → store only the occupied cells in a hash map; the win check then only looks at the lines through the last move. - *"How would you let two players play over the network?"* → the server owns the board and validates the moves — exactly the `move` method above. **Common mistakes:** - ❌ Checking the whole board for a winner after every move instead of only the lines through the last move. - ❌ Forgetting to flip the player after a **winning** move (harmless here, but it breaks the "game over" check). - ❌ Not detecting the draw — the board can be full without a winner. - ❌ Accepting a move on a cell that is already taken. **How to narrate:** > "The state is a 3×3 board plus whose turn it is. There are only eight winning lines, > and after a move only the player who just moved can have won, so I check those eight > triples. The board is flattened into an int[9] so a line is just three indices. I also > keep a `finished` flag so moves after a win or a draw are rejected." ## Related Problems - [Design Browser History — LeetCode 348](./DesignBrowserHistory.md) — a small state machine with an explicit cursor - [Min Max Stack](./MinMaxStack.md) — a structure with its own "terminal" states
